Clonal expansion of malignant uveal melanocytes forms the primary intraocular tumor.
Growing uveal tumor mass disrupts overlying Bruch's membrane and retinal pigment epithelium, causing serous subretinal fluid leakage.
Subretinal serous fluid accumulation separates the neurosensory retina from the retinal pigment epithelium.
Subretinal fluid and tumor mass distortion near the macula or visual axis reduce central visual acuity.
Serous retinal detachment and intraocular mass effect produce a corresponding visual field shadow.

Loss of chromosome 3 deletes the remaining BAP1 allele on 3p21.1, completing biallelic BAP1 tumor-suppressor inactivation.
In germline MBD4 loss-of-function carriers, somatic monosomy 3 eliminates the wild-type MBD4 allele on 3q21.3 in tumor cells.
Loss of BAP1 promotes hematogenous micrometastatic dissemination and outgrowth in the liver.
SF3B1-mutant uveal melanomas carry an intermediate risk of delayed hematogenous liver metastasis.
Accompanies clonal progression of disomy-3 primary uveal melanomas characterized by low metastatic potential, without demonstrated acceleration of melanocyte proliferation.
Outgrowth of hepatic micrometastases produces clinically and radiologically overt liver metastases.
Loss of MBD4 glycosylase activity leaves deaminated 5-methylcytosine G:T mismatches unrepaired, generating widespread CpG>TpG transitions.
Ongoing MBD4-related CpG>TpG mutagenesis accompanies polyphyletic clonal evolution during metastatic progression in monosomy-3 uveal melanoma.

evidence.reference_title: Frequent mutation of BAP1 in metastasizing uveal melanomas.
evidence.snippet: Inactivating somatic mutations were identified in the gene encoding BRCA1-associated protein 1 (BAP1) on chromosome 3p21.1 in 26 of 31 (84%) metastasizing tumors, including 15 mutations causing premature protein termination and 5 affecting its ubiquitin carboxyl-terminal hydrolase domain.

evidence.reference_title: Germline Cancer Susceptibility Variants in Patients With Uveal Melanoma
evidence.snippet: Some patients with uveal melanoma (UM) show genetic cancer predisposition: ~2% harbor a pathogenic or likely pathogenic (P/LP) germline variant in BAP1 or, rarely, in 20 other cancer‐associated genes.

nodes.description: BAP1 (BRCA1-associated protein 1) on chromosome 3p21.1 encodes a nuclear ubiquitin carboxyl-terminal hydrolase (cysteine-type deubiquitinase) involved in chromatin remodeling and transcriptional regulation. Biallelic BAP1 inactivation—typically combining somatic loss-of-function mutation with monosomy 3—occurs in over 80% of metastasizing uveal melanomas, driving a dedifferentiated class 2 transcriptional program and hematogenous dissemination.

nodes.description: GNAQ and GNA11 encode alpha subunits of heterotrimeric Gq/11 G-proteins. Somatic missense mutations at Q209 (most common) or R183 impair intrinsic GTPase activity, locking the subunit in a constitutively active GTP-bound state and driving persistent downstream signaling. These mutations are mutually exclusive early initiating events in uveal melanomagenesis.

evidence.snippet: Codon 183 in both GNA11 and GNAQ is located within the guanosine triphosphate binding region of the human Gα subunit, a region required for hydrolysis of guanosine triphosphate to guanosine diphosphate and an essential step for inactivation of G-protein coupled receptor signaling. Therefore, these mutations lead to decreased function of guanosine triphosphatase and to constitutive activation of downstream effector pathways.

nodes.description: Whole-chromosome loss of one copy of chromosome 3 (monosomy 3, or acquired isodisomy 3) is the defining cytogenetic bifurcation separating high-risk metastasizing uveal melanomas from low-risk disomy-3 tumors. Because both BAP1 (3p21.1) and MBD4 (3q21.3) reside on chromosome 3, monosomy 3 removes the wild-type allele to complete biallelic inactivation of somatic BAP1 mutations and, in germline MBD4 variant carriers, biallelic MBD4 loss.
